paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God wants you to turn and live. Israel's people said their sins were so heavy they were wasting away, and they asked, "How can we live?" God answered with an oath: "As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked should turn from their ways and live." (Ezekiel 33:10-11). That is the heart of the whole passage, and it's good news. The door back to God is open, and He is the One holding it.

Now, what you've done before doesn't lock you in either direction. A wicked man who turns and does what is just and right, "None of the sins he has committed will be held against him." (Ezekiel 33:16). But a righteous man who trusts in his own righteousness and then commits iniquity finds that "none of his righteous works will be remembered" (Ezekiel 33:13). So the plaque on the wall can't carry you, and the worst chapter of your past can't hold you down. Turning is what matters, and God says it again and again in this passage, so I'm saying it again too: TURN, TURN, TURN!

Then there's the watchman. God made Ezekiel one so that people would hear the warning and have the chance to turn (Ezekiel 33:7). When the horn sounds, the one who hears it has to heed it. And God's people said, "The way of the Lord is not just." He answered, "But it is their way that is not just" (Ezekiel 33:17). So when God's Word warns you, take it as love from the One who wants you alive, and turn while the horn is still sounding.
